newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand share market gives thumbs up to RBNZ.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand share market gives thumbs up to RBNZ.

text.p: * New Zealand share market stages broad-based rally
* NZ dollar falls, interest rates rally sharply
* Market gives thumbs up to monetary policy statement
Price movements at close

New Zealand shares staged a broad-based rally to close 1.37 percent higher on Friday as investors welcomed a new, friendlier, monetary environment set out by the Reserve Bank in its Monetary Policy Statement.

The central bank endorsed the recent market-led easing in monetary conditions, loosening its policy by 100 basis points and signalling it would allow a 50-point deviation in conditions either side of its desired level.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 33.07 points higher at 2,443.22 on hefty turnover worth NZ$97 million.
John Rattray at Ord Minnett said the rally in interest rates and the lower dollar gave the market a much needed shot in the arm and the rally was unusual in that it was very broad-based.
Those with purely domestic exposure performed strongly, as did exporters who will benefit from the the decline in the New Zealand dollar.
"What the market has reacted to is the greater certainty. The market perceives interest rates remaining lower," he said.
"The equity market is susceptible to interest rate moves and there is probably a bit of a perception that we are passing through a trough."

Rattray said the session was distinguished by the breadth of the market's advance. In the recent past, Telecom had been the main driver. "But this one is a very general move. It's very broad-based -- that's the hallmark of it," he said.
All leaders posted significant gains, with the exception of Lion Nathan, which remained at NZ$3.72.
Second line issues made solid headway, with utilities, energy stocks, publishers and manufacturers posting big gains.
